resources.string: Buffering, memory use, and connection settings.
Choose a starting point or restore defaults. Individual changes are saved as Custom.
Restore all network settings to mpvNova and mpv.conf defaults.
Use the original mpvNova or mpv.conf value.
32 MiB ahead, 8 MiB behind, up to 30 seconds. Uses less memory.
64 MiB ahead, 16 MiB behind, up to 2 minutes. A moderate buffer for everyday streaming.
96 MiB ahead, 16 MiB behind, up to 3 minutes. Refills 5 seconds after a stall. Cannot fix a consistently slow server.
256 MiB ahead, 32 MiB behind, up to 3 minutes. More space for large video streams; uses more memory.
Memory limit for video buffered ahead. More can help brief connection drops; it does not make downloads faster. Updates during playback.
Keeps recently played data for faster backward seeks. Set to 0 to keep none. Updates during playback; discarded data must be fetched again.
How far ahead to buffer network streams. The memory limit may be reached sooner. Default fills up to the memory limit. Updates during playback.
Wait for the buffer to refill
Wait for more data after a stall instead of repeatedly stuttering. Updates during playback.
Seconds to buffer after a stall. More can reduce repeated pauses but means a longer wait. Limited by available buffer space. Updates during playback.
Mainly for local files. Network caching uses the larger of this and Buffer ahead, within the memory limit. Updates during playback.
Small low-level input buffer, separate from Video buffer size. Usually best left at Default. Applies when a stream is opened again.
How long to wait for a stalled network operation before giving up. Protocol support varies. Applies when a stream is opened again.
Saved. Stream read buffer and timeout changes take effect when a stream is opened again.
Custom forward and backward buffers are limited to %1$d MiB combined on this device. Reduce the other buffer to free space.
Enter a whole number from %1$s to %2$s.
